notes: §1985:XV.2.1.3 GR2: without WITH DEBUGGING MODE 'any USE FOR DEBUGGING statements and all associated debugging sections are compiled as if they were comment lines'. At 85 (Frontend passes debuggingSectionsAreComments where UseForDebuggingRemoved2002 is available) DebuggingLineRewriter#Rewrite finds each declarative section whose first sentence is USE FOR DEBUGGING (DebuggingSections) and Resolve moves its tokens off the default channel unless the unit or a containing unit declares the mode (§1985:VI.4.3.4 GR1); ProcedureTableBuilder#DeclCollectSection skips such a section as a second guard, and DataBinder#BindDeclarations with ConfigurationStep#Inherit carry the mode into contained programs. Probes at 85: without the mode a debugging section holding an undefined data-name, an undefined ON procedure, 'MOVE TO TO.', an unclosed literal and stray characters compiles and never runs, and a USE AFTER ERROR section beside it still runs after a failed OPEN (35); with the mode the section runs on ALL PROCEDURES, on a paragraph and on ALL REFERENCES (DEBUG-NAME, DEBUG-CONTENTS); a contained program inherits the mode, a separately compiled program after END PROGRAM does not; at 2002/2023 the section is COBOL0902. The witness, without the mode, prints MAIN only. A comment line holds any characters (§1985:III, Comment Line), so the characters *> in such a section are no 2002 floating comment indicator (kb/Work PB5588): SurvivingFloatingComments#Note notes each *> the text stages left in the text, DebuggingLineRewriter#Rewrite reports the text lines it makes comment (a debugging section from its header to the line before the next header, a debugging line, the portion's own header and END DECLARATIVES when only debugging sections stand in it), and Frontend#Parse asks ReferenceFormatDiagnostics#ReportSurvivingFloatingComments for the COBOL0900 only of the ones on other lines; witness pb5588_floating_text_in_debugging_comment_85 (a *> in the section and on a debugging line, no mode: prints MAIN); with the mode the same text is refused (pb5588-floating-on-source-debugging-line-85).

next.reason: 1985: "If the WITH DEBUGGING MODE clause is not specified in the SOURCE-COMPUTER paragraph ... compiled as if they were comment lines"; 2023: "SOURCE-COMPUTER rules cover only computer-name-1 and the source computer; no WITH DEBUGGING MODE or USE FOR DEBUGGING". The 2023 SOURCE-COMPUTER rules no longer mention debugging mode, and no candidate has USE FOR DEBUGGING. The Debug module feature is absent from 2023.
